tools.name: conflicts
tools.description: Says which copy of a resource the game takes, and every copy of it in the order the game looks for it (with each copy's priority, and why the game does not have one where it does not), for one resource (`name`) or every resource more than one source has. The order is the game's, read in the exe, for the campaign, language and texture quality ghilana was started with. Use it to see what an add-in or a mod overrides and what overrides it (`source`: `lost` counts those it does not win), or where a resource comes from.

name.description: One resource: every copy of it. Default: every resource with more than one copy.

source.description: Only resources one of whose copies is in this source: one add-in's or mod's conflicts.

across_sources.description: Only resources whose copies are in more than one source. Default true; false adds a source's own repeats (a core file and its patch).

unused.description: Count and list copies the game does not have too (another campaign's, language's or texture quality's, a disabled add-in's). Default false.

offset.description: How many to skip first, to page through a long answer. Default 0.

tools.name: environment
tools.description: What ghilana is serving: the game install read (and every install found on the machine), the exe's build, the Documents folder and instance, the language, DAOLib and its plugins if installed, and each source of resources (the core, the campaign, every add-in and offer with whether AddIns.xml enables it, the packages a campaign loads ahead of the core such as Awakening's core_ep1, the override folders, DAOLib plugins' overrides) with how many archives and files it holds and how many cannot be read. Call it first. The first call reads every archive's directory (some ten thousand) and says how long that took; later calls are fast.

sources.description: List every source. Default true; false for the summary alone.

tools.name: extract
tools.description: Writes resources out of the game's archives into a folder of yours, by name or pattern, for a tool that wants the files themselves. Answers each file written with its path and the copy it came from, and what could not be (an enciphered add-in's copy). Writes nothing in the game's folders.

to.description: The folder to write into, a full path; made if missing. Never inside the game's folder.

all_copies.description: Write every copy, each into a folder named for its source and then its archive's path. Default false: the copy the game takes.

most.description: The most resources a pattern may match. Default 1000.

tools.name: model
tools.description: Says what a model is made of, from its hierarchy (.mmh) and the mesh file (.msh) it names: its nodes by kind, its bones, and each mesh node's chunk with its material (.mao), vertex and triangle counts, vertex elements, bounds, and whether it is skinned and over how many bones. `tree` lists the nodes. Use `model_export` to open it in Blender.

name.description: The model's hierarchy, "cn_bdy_ogra_0.mmh" (the extension may be left off). `resources` with type mmh finds one; it names its mesh file (.msh) itself.

source.description: Which copy of the .mmh, by its source ("core", "addin:..."). Default: the copy the game takes. Its mesh file is always the game's copy.

archive.description: Which copy of the .mmh, by its archive's path.

tree.description: List every node too: its name, kind, parent and bone index. Default false.

tools.name: model_export
tools.description: Writes a model as glTF 2.0 (<name>.gltf and <name>.bin) into a folder of yours, for Blender's built-in glTF import: its node tree, each mesh with normals, tangents, texture coordinates and colours, and its bones as one skin with each vertex's weights. Z up is made glTF's Y up. The game's names and kinds are kept in each node's and mesh's `extras` ("dao"), which Blender keeps as custom properties. Answers the paths, the counts, and `notes` on anything left out. Textures are not written yet. Writes nothing in the game's folders.

name.description: The model's hierarchy, "cn_bdy_ogra_0.mmh" (the extension may be left off). `resources` with type mmh finds one; it names its mesh file (.msh) itself.

source.description: Which copy of the .mmh, by its source ("core", "addin:..."). Default: the copy the game takes. Its mesh file is always the game's copy.

archive.description: Which copy of the .mmh, by its archive's path.

to.description: The folder to write into, a full path; made if missing. Never inside the game's folder.

tools.name: model_import
tools.description: Writes a model edited in Blender back as the game's files: the glTF's meshes put into the original .msh in place of their chunks (matched by the custom properties `model_export` wrote, else by name), each vertex where the glTF has it at rest, with its normal, tangent and binormal, texture coordinates and its bones by name, and the .mmh with each mesh node's bones and material made to match and its bounding boxes made again. Vertices and triangles may be added, moved or removed. A mesh that is none of the model's chunks, or a copy of one (Blender's duplicate), is added as a new chunk under a new mesh node like the one it was copied from (else the first), with the glTF's material. A joint that is none of the model's bones is added as a new bone under the nearest node above it, where the glTF has it at rest; no animation moves it, so it follows its parent. A mesh weighted to more than 67 bones (the most the game's skinning shaders take for one chunk) is split into chunks of at most 67, the rest under new mesh nodes like its own. Bone moves and textures are not taken. Answers each chunk's counts before and after, the files written, `notes`, and where to put the files for the game to take them. Writes nothing in the game's folders.

name.description: The model the glTF was made from, its hierarchy (.mmh): the one `model_export` wrote it from. Its files are the base the meshes are written into.

source.description: Which copy of the .mmh, by its source ("core", "addin:..."). Default: the copy the game takes. Its mesh file is always the game's copy.

archive.description: Which copy of the .mmh, by its archive's path.

gltf.description: The edited model, a .gltf (with its .bin beside it) or .glb, full path. Export from Blender with custom properties on (export_extras=True), so each mesh still says its chunk.

to.description: The folder to write the .msh and .mmh into, a full path; made if missing. Never inside the game's folder.

tools.name: query
tools.description: Searches every resource of a type across the install by its fields: every creature template with Appearance_Type 80, every item of a base type. GFF3 templates (.utc, .uti, .utp, .utt, .are) and GFF4 files (.plo, .dlg, ...) are read: of each resource the copy the game takes, or every copy with `copies` all. Answers the matches with the fields asked and the copy each is in, a count of all, and with `group_by` the counts by a field's value. Copies in enciphered add-in archives are counted, not searched. `resource` on a match shows its every field.

type.description: The files' extension: utc (creatures), uti (items), utp, plo, dlg, ...

where.description: Fields and the values they must have: {"Appearance_Type": 80}. A bare name is found at the top or in the nearest struct below that has it; a dotted path names one ("Appearance Data.Appearance_Type"). A localised name matches its string id; an array matches any of its values. Default: every file.

fields.description: Fields to answer each match with.

group_by.description: A field: count the matches by its value.

copies.description: game (default): of each resource the copy the game takes; all: every copy, the ones it shadows and does not have too.

depth.description: How deep nested fields are read. Default 6.

items.description: The most elements of a list read. Default 100.

offset.description: How many to skip first, to page through a long answer. Default 0.

tools.name: references
tools.description: What a resource names and what names it. `uses`: every field of the resource (a template, a conversation, a plot, a data table's cells) whose text is another resource's name, with or without its extension, and the string ids it holds. `used_by`: with `used_by_types`, every file of those types with a field naming this resource. Follows a creature to its conversation and scripts, a table row to its models.

used_by_types.description: Search every file of these types for what names this resource: ["utc", "dlg"]. Default: none, which only answers what it names.

archive.description: Which copy, by its archive's path.

limit.description: The most of each list. Default 100.

tools.name: resource
tools.description: Reads one resource and answers what it holds: a GFF4 file (conversation, plot, model, ...) or a GFF3 template (.utc, .uti, .utp) as JSON with its fields named, a data table as columns and rows, a talk table's strings, a texture's size and format, a text file (.mao, .xml, .nss) as text, anything else as its first bytes. Of several copies it reads the one the game takes, and says so with the others; `source` and `archive` name another. A copy in an enciphered add-in archive cannot be read here; the answer says so.

depth.description: How deep to follow nested structs and lists. Default 12.

items.description: The most elements of any one list (and rows of a table). Default 200.

chars.description: The most bytes of a text file. Default 20000.

source.description: Which copy, by its source as answers name it ("core", "addin:dao_prc_cp_1", "plugin:mymod"). Default: the copy the game takes.

archive.description: Which copy, by its archive's path (or a loose file's) as answers give it.

tools.name: resources
tools.description: Finds resources by name across every source of the install: core, campaign, add-ins, offers, override folders and DAOLib plugins' overrides. Answers each name with every copy of it (its source, archive or file, size, and whether it can be read), sorted by name, with the count of all matches. Use it to find a name to pass to `resource`, `texture`, `table` or Eluvian's tools (a creature template for stage_spawn).

match.description: Words that must all be in the name, in any case ("ogre default"), or a pattern with * and ? ("abi_*.gda"). Default: every name.

type.description: An extension: utc, uti, gda, dlg, dds, tlk... Default: all.

source.description: Only resources with a copy in this source ("addin:dao_prc_cp_2"); `environment` lists them.

offset.description: How many to skip first, to page through a long answer. Default 0.

tools.name: strings
tools.description: Turns string ids (strrefs, as templates, tables and conversations hold them) into the game's text, and text into string ids, across every talk table of a language: the core's, the campaign's and each add-in's. With neither, lists the talk tables read.

id.description: A string id (strref), or an array of them: their text.

text.description: Text to find, without case: the ids of the strings holding it.

exact.description: `text` is the whole string, not part of it. Default false.

language.description: en-us, fr-fr, de-de, ... Default: the server's (--language).

female.description: The talk tables a female player's character is spoken to with (_f). Default false.

offset.description: How many to skip first, to page through a long answer. Default 0.

tools.name: table
tools.description: Reads one of the game's data tables merged the way the game merges it (M2DA). The table is built from every GDA file whose name starts with the table's prefix, from every source (for example the core's abi_base.gda and a mod's abi_*.gda), using the copy of each file the game uses. Files are ordered by source, then by name; when two files give the same ID, the game keeps the row from the first. Each row says which file and source it comes from, and `_over` lists the files whose rows for that ID it replaces. Filter with `id` or `where`; use `overrides_only` to see only what mods and add-ins change; page with `limit`/`offset`.

table.description: The table: its number (m2da_base.gda's ID, as the scripts' TABLE_* constants: 1 is Abilities), its worksheet prefix ("abi"), its label ("Abilities"), or a GDA file's name ("abi_base").

id.description: Only the rows of this ID, or these IDs.

where.description: Only rows whose columns have these values: {"Label": "Flurry"}. Text without case.

overrides_only.description: Only the IDs that files give different rows, the row the game keeps of each (with `dropped`, the others too). Default false.

dropped.description: Also the rows the game drops: a later file's row of an ID an earlier file has, marked _dropped. Default false: the table as the game has it.

offset.description: How many to skip first, to page through a long answer. Default 0.

tools.name: texture
tools.description: Shows a DDS texture as a PNG image you can look at, with its size and the copy it came from: one picture of its mip chain no larger than `size`, all its channels or one as grey; `width` and `height` are the picture shown. `file` is what the file holds: its `format` (DXT1, DXT3, DXT5, B8G8R8 or B8G8R8A8, the ones read), its largest picture's size, `mips` (counted from the bytes; `header_mips` where the header says otherwise, as the game's own files often do) and `shape` (flat, cube or volume).

size.description: The most pixels a side: the largest of the texture's pictures (mip levels) no larger. Default 512.

channel.description: Which channels: rgba (default), rgb without alpha, or one of them as grey (alpha as grey shows a mask).

source.description: Which copy, by its source as answers name it ("core", "addin:dao_prc_cp_1", "plugin:mymod"). Default: the copy the game takes.

archive.description: Which copy, by its archive's path (or a loose file's) as answers give it.

tools.name: texture_export
tools.description: Writes a texture (.dds) as a PNG of its largest picture into a folder of yours, for an image editor: red, green, blue and alpha as the game draws them, and a normal map with x, y, z in red, green and blue as an editor shows one. Answers the PNG's path, the original's format and size, and the game's smaller copies for its farther models. `texture_import` puts it back.

name.description: The texture, "cn_bdy_ogra_0d.dds" (the extension may be left off). A material (.mao, `resource` shows one as text) names its textures; `resources` with type dds finds more.

source.description: Which copy, by its source ("core", "addin:..."). Default: the copy the game takes.

archive.description: Which copy, by its archive's path.

to.description: The folder to write into, a full path; made if missing. Never inside the game's folder.

normal.description: Whether it is a normal map, x, y, z in the PNG's red, green and blue. Default: its name ends in n, as the game's do (cn_bdy_ogra_0n).

tools.name: texture_import
tools.description: Writes a PNG edited from `texture_export` back as the game's texture (.dds): in the original's format with every halving of the picture down to a pixel, as the game's own are, and the game's smaller copies for its farther models too. The picture's sides must be powers of two. Answers the files written and where to put them for the game to take them. Writes nothing in the game's folders.

name.description: The texture the PNG replaces, "cn_bdy_ogra_0d.dds": its format is the one written, and its name the file's.

source.description: Which copy, by its source ("core", "addin:..."). Default: the copy the game takes.

archive.description: Which copy, by its archive's path.

to.description: The folder to write into, a full path; made if missing. Never inside the game's folder.

png.description: The edited picture, a PNG's full path.

normal.description: Whether it is a normal map, x, y, z in the PNG's red, green and blue. Default: its name ends in n, as the game's do (cn_bdy_ogra_0n).

format.description: The DDS format to write. Default: the original's (DXT3 becomes DXT5, 24 bits 32).

far_copies.description: Also write the game's smaller copies for its farther models (..._0dl2, _0dl3), from the picture halved. Default true.
